Channel 3 (obstacles) is high on the outer border, as expected, and has only sparse low interior structure, e.g. (r1,c7), (r2,c2), (r3,c6), (r4,c2), (r5,c6), (r8,c2), (r8,c6) â consistent with a fixed maze of walls. The output layer is omitted, but the 500 inputs and 5 actions match a 10Ã10Ã5 MinAtar observation.

Reasoning: The 10Ã10 grid with 5 binary channels, 5 actions, and the exact parameter count 17,253 all point to the MinAtar benchmark. Among MinAtar games, only Asterix has the channel set: agent, moving enemies, treasure/reward target, walls/obstacles, and previous frame. The reward-target map being concentrated on the top row matches Asterixâs treasure appearing at the top. The moving-object map showing row-wise enemy lanes matches Asterixâs horizontally moving enemies. The obstacle map showing a mostly empty interior with a few wall cells matches Asterixâs sparse maze. Games like Breakout, Freeway, Seaquest, and SpaceInvaders lack this combination: Breakout has no moving enemies or walls; Freeway has no reward targets or walls; Seaquest has no interior walls and different reward semantics; SpaceInvaders has no walls or top-row treasure.

Game: Asterix (MinAtar version, based on the Atari 2600 game Asterix).

Description: The agent controls a character starting near the bottom of an 8Ã8 playable maze. It must avoid horizontally moving enemies and navigate around fixed wall obstacles while moving upward to collect a treasure that appears in the top row, which provides reward.

Confidence: 95%
